Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 65, verse 1–3:

(Surat al-Talaq is Madani, and it has twelve verses.)

(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.)

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed period, and count the period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter.﴾ ﴿Then when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men from among you, and establish the testimony for Allah. That is what is admonished to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out.﴾ ﴿And will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah – then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set a measure for everything.﴾.

(This surah is Madani. It is said: the occasion of its revelation was the divorce of Hafsah by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), related by Qatadah from Anas. Al-Suddi said: it was the divorce by Abdullah ibn Amr. It is also said: some people did the same as his action, among them Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, Amr ibn Sa'id ibn al-As, and Utbah ibn Ghazwan, so it was revealed. Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: although this is not authentic, the first view is the better, and the most correct position regarding it is that it is an explanation of a newly instituted law. Its connection with what precedes it: when He mentioned the trial of wealth and children, He pointed to the trial through women, that they may put men to trial until one finds no escape from it except through divorce. So He mentioned that one separates from them in a good manner, by not having any continued relation between them, neither seeking a child nor a pregnancy.)

﴿O Prophet﴾: a call to the Prophet (ﷺ), and an address in the manner of honour and alerting. ﴿When you divorce﴾: an address to him – peace be upon him – in the plural form as a mark of respect; or to his community by way of shifting the address (talwin al-khitab); he addressed him first and then returned to them with the address; or by the implied "say" (idmar al-qawl), meaning: say to your community, "When you divorce"; or it is addressed to him and to his community. And it seems there is an omitted element, its estimate being: "O Prophet and the community of the Prophet, when you divorce", so the address is to him and to them, that is, you and your community – these are the opinions. Al-Zamakhshari said: He specified the Prophet (ﷺ) and generalised the address, because the Prophet is the imam and exemplar of his community, as is said to the chief and elder of a people: "O so-and-so, do such-and-such," to show his precedence and to acknowledge his leadership, that he is the spokesman and tongue of his people, the one from whose opinion they proceed and whom they do not single out for a matter apart from him; so he alone is in the position of all of them and stands in place of all of them. End of quote; and it is a fine statement.

The meaning of ﴿when you divorce﴾ is: when you intend to divorce them. "Women" refers to those with whom intercourse has taken place. (So divorce them) means: effect the divorce (for their prescribed period): this is by elision of a noun, meaning: at the onset of their prescribed period; and the lam indicates a specific time, as in: "I wrote it for a night remaining of the month of such-and-such." Al-Zamakhshari's estimate here, of an omitted circumstantial phrase indicated by the meaning to which the prepositional phrase relates, meaning "beginning their prescribed period," is not good, because he estimated a specific governing word, and the governing word in an adverbial or prepositional phrase is not omitted when it is specific, but only when it is a general predicate. If you say, "Zayd is with you" or "in the house," meaning "laughing with you" or "laughing in the house," it is not permitted. So attaching the lam to the verb ﴿divorce them﴾ with an elided noun is the correct view. What has been related from a group of the Companions and the Successors – may Allah be pleased with them – that they recited "divorce them at the beginning of their prescribed period" (fi qubuli 'iddatihinna), and from some of them, "at the side of their prescribed period" (fi qibali 'iddatihinna), and from Abdullah: "for the beginning of their purity" (liqibali tuhrihinna), these are by way of explanation, not as Qur'an, because they contradict the consonantal text of the codex on which the Muslims unanimously agreed, east and west.

Is the prescribed period reckoned by purities or by menstruation? This was discussed in al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228]. The intended meaning is that he divorces them in a purity in which he has not had intercourse with them, then they are left until their prescribed period ends; if he wishes he takes them back, and if he wishes he lets them go, so that they are free to remarry. This form of divorce is the more included in the Sunnah. Malik said: I know of no divorce of the Sunnah except a single one, and he disliked three pronounced together or separately. Abu Hanifah disliked more than one in a single purity, but separately in purities is not objectionable. Al-Shafi'i said: there is no harm in sending three divorces, and I know of no Sunnah or innovation in the number of divorces; it is permitted; he considered only the time in the Sunnah, whereas Abu Hanifah considered both separation and time. His saying ﴿divorce them﴾ is unrestricted, with no reference to a number or to a description of separation or joining. The majority hold that if he divorces contrary to the Sunnah, it takes effect. It is related from Ibn al-Musayyib and a group of the Successors that if he divorces during menstruation or three times, it does not take effect. The apparent sense is that the address in ﴿and count the period﴾ is to the husbands, that is: keep precise account. There are benefits in counting: observing the right of retraction, the time of maintenance and lodging, distributing the divorces over the periods, and when he intends to divorce three times, knowing that she has become separated, so that he may marry her sister or four others besides her. He – exalted is He – forbade expelling them from their dwellings until the prescribed period ends, and He forbade them also from leaving; He attributed the houses to them because they dwell in them, and their being forbidden to leave is not permitted by the husband's permission, since his permission has no effect. Maintenance is incumbent on the husband: if the house is his property or rented, that suffices; or if it is her property, then he owes her its rent. This applies equally to a revocable divorce and an irrevocable one. The Sunnah in this matter is that she should not spend the night away from her house, nor leave it by day except out of necessity, for the preservation of lineage and the safeguarding of women.

﴿Unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: it is adultery, according to Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, Ikrimah, Hammad and al-Layth, and Mujahid related it from Ibn Abbas; so they go out for the prescribed punishment. From Ibn Abbas: abuse directed at the in-laws; then she may leave, and her right to maintenance falls away, and she is obliged to reside in a dwelling she acquires for the preservation of lineage. Also from him: all sins, such as theft, slander, adultery, or other things; this was chosen by al-Tabari, and her right to maintenance then falls away. According to Ibn Umar, al-Suddi and Ibn al-Sa'ib: it is her leaving her house as a permanent removal, so her right to maintenance falls away. Also according to Qatadah: her rebellion (nushuz) against the husband, so she is divorced on account of that, and he owes her no maintenance. If her right to maintenance falls away, she completes the prescribed period.

﴿You do not know﴾, O listener, ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾. The commentators said: the matter here is the desire to take her back and the inclination toward her after having turned away from her, or the appearance of a pregnancy, so that he takes her back on its account. "You do not know" is in the accusative as a clause expressing hope, so "you do not know" is suspended from operating; we have previously discussed His saying: ﴿and I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111], and we mentioned that "perhaps" (la'alla) should be added to the suspending verbs. Thus the clause expressing hope is in the accusative position governed by "you do not know."

﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾: that is, they have come near the end of the prescribed period; ﴿retain them﴾: that is, take them back; ﴿in kindness﴾: without harm. ﴿Or part from them in kindness﴾: that is, release them with goodness. The meaning is: leave them until their prescribed period ends, so that they have authority over themselves. al-Jumhur read "ajalahunna" in the singular; al-Dahhak and Ibn Sirin read "ajalahunna" in the plural. Retaining in kindness is good companionship in what the wife is owed from the husband; parting in kindness is the payment of the dower, the provision (mut'ah), the obligatory rights, and fulfilment of stipulations. ﴿And call to witness﴾: the apparent sense is that calling witnesses is obligatory for what occurs of retention, which is the return, or separation, which is divorce. This calling of witnesses is recommended according to Abu Hanifah, like His saying: ﴿and call witnesses when you trade﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. According to the Shafi'is it is obligatory for the return and recommended for the separation. It is also said: "call to witness" refers to the return only, and witnessing is a condition for its validity, so she may withhold herself from him until he calls witnesses. Ibn Abbas said: calling witnesses to the return and to the divorce removes many kinds of disputes and prevents confusion about the date of the witnessing. It is said: the benefit of witnessing is that no mutual denial arises between them, that he is not suspected of retaining her, and that if one of them dies, the other does not claim the existence of the marriage in order to inherit. End of quote. The meaning of ﴿from among you﴾: al-Hasan said: from the Muslims; Qatadah said: from the free.

﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾: this is a command to the witnesses, that is, for the sake of Allah alone, not for the benefit of any party witnessed for, nor witnessed against, looking only to upholding the truth. ﴿That﴾ refers to the establishing of testimony, since the events of matters revolve around it, and by it the falsifier is distinguished from the truthful.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talib and a group said: it is in the sense of divorce, that is, whoever does not exceed the divorce of the Sunnah to the divorce of three or otherwise, Allah will make for him a way out if he regrets and returns; ﴿and will provide for him﴾: what feeds his family. End of quote. The implication of the condition is that if he does not fear Allah, and he issues an irrevocable divorce and then regrets, he will have no way out, and his wife's provision will cease from him. Ibn Abbas said to one who divorced three times: "You did not fear Allah; your wife has been separated from you, and I see no way out for you." He also said: ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾ means He will deliver him from the distresses of this world and the Hereafter. The apparent sense is that His saying ﴿whoever fears Allah﴾ is connected with the command of what preceded concerning rulings of divorce. It is related that it has another sense: a son named Salim was taken captive by Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, "so he complained of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded him to be mindful of Allah, and he accepted; then not long after, his son escaped and drove off a hundred camels." This is as in al-Kashshaf. In al-Wajiz: "a herd of sheep which belonged to those who had captured him"; and he came to his father and asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Is it lawful for him?" He said: "Yes," and the verse was revealed. al-Dahhak said: ﴿from where he does not expect﴾ means another woman. It is also said: whoever fears the forbidden, Allah will make for him a way out to the lawful. It is said: a way out from hardship to ease. It is said: from the Fire to Paradise. It is said: from punishment, and He will provide him from where he does not expect, from reward. al-Kalbi said: whoever fears Allah at the time of calamity, Allah will make for him a way out to Paradise.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾: that is, entrusts his affair to Him; ﴿then He is sufficient for him﴾: that is, sufficient for him.

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾: Masruq said: that is, the command of Allah must be executed, whether you rely upon Him or not. al-Jumhur read "bali'un" with tanwin and "amrahu" in the accusative. Ibn Abi Abla also, Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Isma, from Abu Amr, read "bali'un amruhu" with the nominative, meaning: His command is effective. al-Mufaddal also read "balighan" with the accusative and "amruhu" with the nominative; al-Zamakhshari explained it as: "balighan" is a circumstantial accusative, and the predicate of "inna" is His saying ﴿Allah has already set﴾. It may also be explained according to the view of those who put both parts in the accusative after "inna," as in the poet's verse:

"When the darkness of night grows black, let you come, and let your steps be light, for our guards are lions."

As for whoever reads "amruhu" in the nominative, the object of "balighun" is omitted, its estimate being: "accomplishing His command whatever He wills."

﴿Allah has already set a measure for everything﴾: that is, a determination and a fixed term that it does not exceed. These clauses urge reliance upon Allah. Jannah ibn Hubaysh read "qadaran" with a fatha on the dal, while the majority read it with sukun.

Its connection with what precedes it: when He mentioned the trial of wealth and children, He pointed to the trial through women, that they may put men to trial until one finds no escape from it except through divorce. So He mentioned that one separates from them in a good manner, by not having any continued relation between them, neither seeking a child nor a pregnancy.)

﴿O Prophet﴾: a call to the Prophet (ﷺ), and an address in the manner of honour and alerting. ﴿When you divorce﴾: an address to him – peace be upon him – in the plural form as a mark of respect; or to his community by way of shifting the address (talwin al-khitab); he addressed him first and then returned to them with the address; or by the implied "say" (idmar al-qawl), meaning: say to your community, "When you divorce"; or it is addressed to him and to his community. And it seems there is an omitted element, its estimate being: "O Prophet and the community of the Prophet, when you divorce", so the address is to him and to them, that is, you and your community – these are the opinions. Al-Zamakhshari said: He specified the Prophet (ﷺ) and generalised the address, because the Prophet is the imam and exemplar of his community, as is said to the chief and elder of a people: "O so-and-so, do such-and-such," to show his precedence and to acknowledge his leadership, that he is the spokesman and tongue of his people, the one from whose opinion they proceed and whom they do not single out for a matter apart from him; so he alone is in the position of all of them and stands in place of all of them. End of quote; and it is a fine statement.

The meaning of ﴿when you divorce﴾ is: when you intend to divorce them. "Women" refers to those with whom intercourse has taken place. (So divorce them) means: effect the divorce (for their prescribed period): this is by elision of a noun, meaning: at the onset of their prescribed period; and the lam indicates a specific time, as in: "I wrote it for a night remaining of the month of such-and-such." Al-Zamakhshari's estimate here, of an omitted circumstantial phrase indicated by the meaning to which the prepositional phrase relates, meaning "beginning their prescribed period," is not good, because he estimated a specific governing word, and the governing word in an adverbial or prepositional phrase is not omitted when it is specific, but only when it is a general predicate. If you say, "Zayd is with you" or "in the house," meaning "laughing with you" or "laughing in the house," it is not permitted. So attaching the lam to the verb ﴿divorce them﴾ with an elided noun is the correct view. What has been related from a group of the Companions and the Successors – may Allah be pleased with them – that they recited "divorce them at the beginning of their prescribed period" (fi qubuli 'iddatihinna), and from some of them, "at the side of their prescribed period" (fi qibali 'iddatihinna), and from Abdullah: "for the beginning of their purity" (liqibali tuhrihinna), these are by way of explanation, not as Qur'an, because they contradict the consonantal text of the codex on which the Muslims unanimously agreed, east and west.

Is the prescribed period reckoned by purities or by menstruation? This was discussed in al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228]. The intended meaning is that he divorces them in a purity in which he has not had intercourse with them, then they are left until their prescribed period ends; if he wishes he takes them back, and if he wishes he lets them go, so that they are free to remarry. This form of divorce is the more included in the Sunnah. Malik said: I know of no divorce of the Sunnah except a single one, and he disliked three pronounced together or separately. Abu Hanifah disliked more than one in a single purity, but separately in purities is not objectionable. Al-Shafi'i said: there is no harm in sending three divorces, and I know of no Sunnah or innovation in the number of divorces; it is permitted; he considered only the time in the Sunnah, whereas Abu Hanifah considered both separation and time. His saying ﴿divorce them﴾ is unrestricted, with no reference to a number or to a description of separation or joining. The majority hold that if he divorces contrary to the Sunnah, it takes effect. It is related from Ibn al-Musayyib and a group of the Successors that if he divorces during menstruation or three times, it does not take effect. The apparent sense is that the address in ﴿and count the period﴾ is to the husbands, that is: keep precise account. There are benefits in counting: observing the right of retraction, the time of maintenance and lodging, distributing the divorces over the periods, and when he intends to divorce three times, knowing that she has become separated, so that he may marry her sister or four others besides her. He – exalted is He – forbade expelling them from their dwellings until the prescribed period ends, and He forbade them also from leaving; He attributed the houses to them because they dwell in them, and their being forbidden to leave is not permitted by the husband's permission, since his permission has no effect. Maintenance is incumbent on the husband: if the house is his property or rented, that suffices; or if it is her property, then he owes her its rent. This applies equally to a revocable divorce and an irrevocable one. The Sunnah in this matter is that she should not spend the night away from her house, nor leave it by day except out of necessity, for the preservation of lineage and the safeguarding of women.

﴿Unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: it is adultery, according to Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, Ikrimah, Hammad and al-Layth, and Mujahid related it from Ibn Abbas; so they go out for the prescribed punishment. From Ibn Abbas: abuse directed at the in-laws; then she may leave, and her right to maintenance falls away, and she is obliged to reside in a dwelling she acquires for the preservation of lineage. Also from him: all sins, such as theft, slander, adultery, or other things; this was chosen by al-Tabari, and her right to maintenance then falls away. According to Ibn Umar, al-Suddi and Ibn al-Sa'ib: it is her leaving her house as a permanent removal, so her right to maintenance falls away. Also according to Qatadah: her rebellion (nushuz) against the husband, so she is divorced on account of that, and he owes her no maintenance. If her right to maintenance falls away, she completes the prescribed period.

﴿You do not know﴾, O listener, ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾. The commentators said: the matter here is the desire to take her back and the inclination toward her after having turned away from her, or the appearance of a pregnancy, so that he takes her back on its account. "You do not know" is in the accusative as a clause expressing hope, so "you do not know" is suspended from operating; we have previously discussed His saying: ﴿and I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ [al-Anbiya': 111], and we mentioned that "perhaps" (la'alla) should be added to the suspending verbs. Thus the clause expressing hope is in the accusative position governed by "you do not know."

﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾: that is, they have come near the end of the prescribed period; ﴿retain them﴾: that is, take them back; ﴿in kindness﴾: without harm. ﴿Or part from them in kindness﴾: that is, release them with goodness. The meaning is: leave them until their prescribed period ends, so that they have authority over themselves. al-Jumhur read "ajalahunna" in the singular; al-Dahhak and Ibn Sirin read "ajalahunna" in the plural. Retaining in kindness is good companionship in what the wife is owed from the husband; parting in kindness is the payment of the dower, the provision (mut'ah), the obligatory rights, and fulfilment of stipulations. ﴿And call to witness﴾: the apparent sense is that calling witnesses is obligatory for what occurs of retention, which is the return, or separation, which is divorce. This calling of witnesses is recommended according to Abu Hanifah, like His saying: ﴿and call witnesses when you trade﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. According to the Shafi'is it is obligatory for the return and recommended for the separation. It is also said: "call to witness" refers to the return only, and witnessing is a condition for its validity, so she may withhold herself from him until he calls witnesses. Ibn Abbas said: calling witnesses to the return and to the divorce removes many kinds of disputes and prevents confusion about the date of the witnessing. It is said: the benefit of witnessing is that no mutual denial arises between them, that he is not suspected of retaining her, and that if one of them dies, the other does not claim the existence of the marriage in order to inherit. End of quote. The meaning of ﴿from among you﴾: al-Hasan said: from the Muslims; Qatadah said: from the free.

﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾: this is a command to the witnesses, that is, for the sake of Allah alone, not for the benefit of any party witnessed for, nor witnessed against, looking only to upholding the truth. ﴿That﴾ refers to the establishing of testimony, since the events of matters revolve around it, and by it the falsifier is distinguished from the truthful.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talib and a group said: it is in the sense of divorce, that is, whoever does not exceed the divorce of the Sunnah to the divorce of three or otherwise, Allah will make for him a way out if he regrets and returns; ﴿and will provide for him﴾: what feeds his family. End of quote. The implication of the condition is that if he does not fear Allah, and he issues an irrevocable divorce and then regrets, he will have no way out, and his wife's provision will cease from him. Ibn Abbas said to one who divorced three times: "You did not fear Allah; your wife has been separated from you, and I see no way out for you." He also said: ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾ means He will deliver him from the distresses of this world and the Hereafter. The apparent sense is that His saying ﴿whoever fears Allah﴾ is connected with the command of what preceded concerning rulings of divorce. It is related that it has another sense: a son named Salim was taken captive by Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, "so he complained of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he commanded him to be mindful of Allah, and he accepted; then not long after, his son escaped and drove off a hundred camels." This is as in al-Kashshaf. In al-Wajiz: "a herd of sheep which belonged to those who had captured him"; and he came to his father and asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Is it lawful for him?" He said: "Yes," and the verse was revealed. al-Dahhak said: ﴿from where he does not expect﴾ means another woman. It is also said: whoever fears the forbidden, Allah will make for him a way out to the lawful. It is said: a way out from hardship to ease. It is said: from the Fire to Paradise. It is said: from punishment, and He will provide him from where he does not expect, from reward. al-Kalbi said: whoever fears Allah at the time of calamity, Allah will make for him a way out to Paradise.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾: that is, entrusts his affair to Him; ﴿then He is sufficient for him﴾: that is, sufficient for him.

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾: Masruq said: that is, the command of Allah must be executed, whether you rely upon Him or not. al-Jumhur read "bali'un" with tanwin and "amrahu" in the accusative. Ibn Abi Abla also, Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Isma, from Abu Amr, read "bali'un amruhu" with the nominative, meaning: His command is effective. al-Mufaddal also read "balighan" with the accusative and "amruhu" with the nominative; al-Zamakhshari explained it as: "balighan" is a circumstantial accusative, and the predicate of "inna" is His saying ﴿Allah has already set﴾. It may also be explained according to the view of those who put both parts in the accusative after "inna," as in the poet's verse:

As for whoever reads "amruhu" in the nominative, the object of "balighun" is omitted, its estimate being: "accomplishing His command whatever He wills."

﴿Allah has already set a measure for everything﴾: that is, a determination and a fixed term that it does not exceed. These clauses urge reliance upon Allah. Jannah ibn Hubaysh read "qadaran" with a fatha on the dal, while the majority read it with sukun.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 65, verses 8–12:**

His, the Exalted and Majestic's, saying: ﴿How many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe reckoning and punished it with a dreadful punishment. So it tasted the consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss. God has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear God, O people of understanding who have believed. God has sent down to you a reminder, a messenger who recites to you God's clear signs, to bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light. Whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. God has indeed granted him a goodly provision. God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends among them, so that you may know that God is capable of all things and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾

The discussion of ﴿ka'ayyin﴾ (how many) has already been covered in Al 'Imran, and of ﴿nukran﴾ (dreadful) in al-Kahf. ﴿'Atat﴾ means "turned away," ﴿'an amri rabbiha﴾ (from the command of its Lord) out of obstinacy and arrogance. The apparent meaning of ﴿fa-hasabnaha﴾ (so We called it to account) and the four clauses that follow is that this occurs in this world, because of His saying after them: ﴿God has prepared for them a severe punishment.﴾ Its apparent meaning is that what is prepared is the punishment of the Hereafter. The "severe reckoning" (ḥisab shadid) is thorough scrutiny and examination, such that no lapse is overlooked, and they were held to account even for the smallest of sins. It has also been said that the four clauses (reckoning, punishment, tasting, and loss) refer to the Hereafter, and that they are stated in the past tense, as in His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. In this reading, His saying ﴿God has prepared for them﴾ is a repetition of the threat and a clarification that it is awaited, as though He had said, "God has prepared for them this punishment." Al-Kalbi said: the reckoning is in the Hereafter, and the dreadful punishment is in this world, through hunger, famine, and the sword.

When He mentioned what befell this rebellious town, He commanded the believers to fear God, warning them of His punishment, and He drew attention to what urges one toward taqwa (God-consciousness), which is the sending down of the Reminder (dhikr). The apparent meaning is that the Reminder is the Qur'an, and that the Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ). Either the Reminder itself is taken metaphorically, due to the abundance of the reminder that is derived from it, so that it is as if it were the Reminder itself; or the Messenger is a substitute (badal) with an omitted annexed noun (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning "the reminder of a messenger." It has also been said that ﴿rasulan﴾ (a messenger) is a qualifier with an omitted annexed noun, meaning "a reminder that is [a reminder of] a messenger." It has also been said that the annexed noun is omitted from the first term, meaning "a possessor of reminder, a messenger," so that ﴿rasulan﴾ is a qualifier of that omitted noun or a substitute. It has also been said that ﴿rasul﴾ here means "message," so it is a substitute for ﴿dhikr﴾; but His following saying ﴿who recites to you﴾ makes this unlikely, since recitation is attributed to a message only figuratively. It has also been said that the Reminder is the foundation of the names of the Prophet (ﷺ). It has also been said that the Reminder means honour, based on His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. In that case ﴿rasulan﴾ is a substitute for it and an explanation of it.

Al-Kalbi said: the Messenger here is Jibril (peace be upon him), and al-Zamakhshari followed him, saying: "﴿rasulan﴾ is Jibril, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him; it is a substitute for ﴿dhikran﴾ because it is described as reciting God's signs, so his sending down is in the sense of the sending down of the Reminder, and therefore his substitution for it is valid." End of quotation. This does not hold, because the two referents are different in reality, and because it would be neither a substitute of part nor a substitute of inclusion. These grammatical constructions only work if "reminder" and "messenger" refer to one and the same thing.

It has also been said that ﴿rasulan﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an omitted verb, meaning "He sent a messenger" or "He dispatched a messenger," and the verb was omitted because the preceding ﴿anzala﴾ (sent down) indicates it. Al-Suddi took this view, and Ibn 'Atiyyah preferred it. Al-Zajjaj and Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: ﴿rasulan﴾ may be an object governed by the verbal noun that is the Reminder (dhikr). End of quotation. In that case the verbal noun is taken as being with "an" (that) implied, and the sense is "that he mentioned a messenger," and it operates with tanwin (nunation), as it does in His saying ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14], and as the poet said:

*By striking with swords the heads of a people, We removed their skulls from their resting place.*

It is also read as ﴿rasulun﴾ (in the nominative), with an implied pronoun ("he is a messenger"). The clause ﴿li-yukhrija﴾ (to bring out) may be connected with ﴿yatlu﴾ (recites) or with ﴿anzala﴾ (sent down).

﴿Those who believed﴾: that is, those whose faith God had decreed, willed, and determined; or the term "believed" is applied to them in consideration of what their situation came to be. Al-Zamakhshari said: "so that they may attain what they now have of faith and righteous deeds, because at the time of its sending down they were not believers, and they believed only after the sending down and the conveying." End of quotation. The pronoun in ﴿li-yukhrija﴾ refers either to God the Exalted, or to the Messenger (ﷺ), or to the Reminder.

﴿And whoever believes﴾: He observed the wording first with the conditional "whoever" (man), so the pronoun in ﴿yu'min﴾ (believes), ﴿ya'mal﴾ (does), and ﴿yudkhilhu﴾ (admits him) is singular. Then He observed the meaning in ﴿khalidina﴾ (abiding), and then the wording again in ﴿qad ahsana Allahu lahu﴾ (God has indeed granted him), which is singular. Grammarians have cited this verse as evidence for observing the wording first, then the meaning, then the wording again. Some have objected that this is not as they described, because the pronoun in ﴿khalidina﴾ does not refer back to ﴿man﴾, unlike the pronouns in ﴿yu'min﴾, ﴿ya'mal﴾, and ﴿yudkhilhu﴾. Rather, it refers to the object of ﴿yudkhilhu﴾, and ﴿khalidina﴾ is a circumstantial state (hal) of it, and the governing element of that state is ﴿yudkhilhu﴾, not the conditional verb.

﴿God is He who created seven heavens﴾: There is no disagreement that the heavens are seven, by the explicit text of the Qur'an and the hadith, as came in the hadith of the Night Journey, and as in His (ﷺ) saying to Sa'd: "You have judged by the judgment of the King from above seven heavens," and other texts of the Law.

The majority read ﴿mithlahunna﴾ (the like of them) in the accusative. Al-Mufaddal from 'Asim, and 'Isma from Abu Bakr, read ﴿mithluhunna﴾ in the nominative and then the accusative. Al-Zamakhshari said: "it is coordinated with ﴿seven heavens﴾." End of quotation. This involves separating the conjunction (the waw) from the conjoined term by a prepositional phrase, which is considered permissible only in poetic necessity according to Abu 'Ali al-Farisi. Some grammarians supposed a governing verb after the waw, indicated by what precedes it, meaning "and He created of the earth the like of them," so ﴿mithlahunna﴾ is the object of the omitted verb, not a coordinated term, and this becomes coordination of clauses. The nominative reading is on the basis of the inchoative, with ﴿min al-ardi﴾ (of the earth) as the predicate.

The sense of likeness can be true through sharing some attributes. The majority said that the likeness is in number, meaning that they are like them in being seven earths. In the hadith: "He will be hung with a collar from seven earths," and "Lord of the seven earths and what they carry." It was said: they are seven layers without gaps. It was said: there is a distance between each layer and the next. It was said: in them are inhabitants of God's creation. It was said: angels and jinn. On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, from the narration of al-Waqidi the liar, he said: "In every earth there is an Adam like Adam, a Noah like Noah, a prophet like your prophet, an Abraham like your Abraham, and a Jesus like Jesus." This is a narration with no doubt about its being fabricated. Abu Salih said: they are seven earths spread out, none above another, separated by seas, and the sky shades all of them.

﴿The command descends among them﴾: from the seven heavens to the seven earths. Muqatil and others said: the command here is revelation, so "among them" refers to the space between this earth, which is the nearest of them, and the seventh heaven. Most scholars said: the command is the decree, so "among them" refers to the space between the lowest earth, which is the farthest, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was also said: "the command descends among them" refers to life and death, wealth and poverty. It was also said: it is what is administered within them of wondrous governance.

The majority read ﴿yatanazzalu﴾ (descends), the present tense of tanazzala. 'Isa and Abu 'Amr, and in one narration, read ﴿yunazzilu﴾, the present tense of the doubled form nazzala, with ﴿al-amr﴾ (the command) in the accusative. The majority read ﴿li-ta'lamu﴾ (that you may know) with the second-person "ta." It is also read with the third-person "ya," and God knows best.

It has also been said that the four clauses (reckoning, punishment, tasting, and loss) refer to the Hereafter, and that they are stated in the past tense, as in His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. In this reading, His saying ﴿God has prepared for them﴾ is a repetition of the threat and a clarification that it is awaited, as though He had said, "God has prepared for them this punishment." Al-Kalbi said: the reckoning is in the Hereafter, and the dreadful punishment is in this world, through hunger, famine, and the sword.

When He mentioned what befell this rebellious town, He commanded the believers to fear God, warning them of His punishment, and He drew attention to what urges one toward taqwa (God-consciousness), which is the sending down of the Reminder (dhikr). The apparent meaning is that the Reminder is the Qur'an, and that the Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ). Either the Reminder itself is taken metaphorically, due to the abundance of the reminder that is derived from it, so that it is as if it were the Reminder itself; or the Messenger is a substitute (badal) with an omitted annexed noun (mudaf mahdhuf), meaning "the reminder of a messenger." It has also been said that ﴿rasulan﴾ (a messenger) is a qualifier with an omitted annexed noun, meaning "a reminder that is [a reminder of] a messenger." It has also been said that the annexed noun is omitted from the first term, meaning "a possessor of reminder, a messenger," so that ﴿rasulan﴾ is a qualifier of that omitted noun or a substitute. It has also been said that ﴿rasul﴾ here means "message," so it is a substitute for ﴿dhikr﴾; but His following saying ﴿who recites to you﴾ makes this unlikely, since recitation is attributed to a message only figuratively. It has also been said that the Reminder is the foundation of the names of the Prophet (ﷺ). It has also been said that the Reminder means honour, based on His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. In that case ﴿rasulan﴾ is a substitute for it and an explanation of it.

Al-Kalbi said: the Messenger here is Jibril (peace be upon him), and al-Zamakhshari followed him, saying: "﴿rasulan﴾ is Jibril, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him; it is a substitute for ﴿dhikran﴾ because it is described as reciting God's signs, so his sending down is in the sense of the sending down of the Reminder, and therefore his substitution for it is valid." End of quotation. This does not hold, because the two referents are different in reality, and because it would be neither a substitute of part nor a substitute of inclusion. These grammatical constructions only work if "reminder" and "messenger" refer to one and the same thing.

It has also been said that ﴿rasulan﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an omitted verb, meaning "He sent a messenger" or "He dispatched a messenger," and the verb was omitted because the preceding ﴿anzala﴾ (sent down) indicates it. Al-Suddi took this view, and Ibn 'Atiyyah preferred it. Al-Zajjaj and Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: ﴿rasulan﴾ may be an object governed by the verbal noun that is the Reminder (dhikr). End of quotation. In that case the verbal noun is taken as being with "an" (that) implied, and the sense is "that he mentioned a messenger," and it operates with tanwin (nunation), as it does in His saying ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14], and as the poet said:

*By striking with swords the heads of a people, We removed their skulls from their resting place.*

It is also read as ﴿rasulun﴾ (in the nominative), with an implied pronoun ("he is a messenger"). The clause ﴿li-yukhrija﴾ (to bring out) may be connected with ﴿yatlu﴾ (recites) or with ﴿anzala﴾ (sent down).

﴿Those who believed﴾: that is, those whose faith God had decreed, willed, and determined; or the term "believed" is applied to them in consideration of what their situation came to be. Al-Zamakhshari said: "so that they may attain what they now have of faith and righteous deeds, because at the time of its sending down they were not believers, and they believed only after the sending down and the conveying." End of quotation. The pronoun in ﴿li-yukhrija﴾ refers either to God the Exalted, or to the Messenger (ﷺ), or to the Reminder.

﴿And whoever believes﴾: He observed the wording first with the conditional "whoever" (man), so the pronoun in ﴿yu'min﴾ (believes), ﴿ya'mal﴾ (does), and ﴿yudkhilhu﴾ (admits him) is singular. Then He observed the meaning in ﴿khalidina﴾ (abiding), and then the wording again in ﴿qad ahsana Allahu lahu﴾ (God has indeed granted him), which is singular. Grammarians have cited this verse as evidence for observing the wording first, then the meaning, then the wording again. Some have objected that this is not as they described, because the pronoun in ﴿khalidina﴾ does not refer back to ﴿man﴾, unlike the pronouns in ﴿yu'min﴾, ﴿ya'mal﴾, and ﴿yudkhilhu﴾. Rather, it refers to the object of ﴿yudkhilhu﴾, and ﴿khalidina﴾ is a circumstantial state (hal) of it, and the governing element of that state is ﴿yudkhilhu﴾, not the conditional verb.

﴿God is He who created seven heavens﴾: There is no disagreement that the heavens are seven, by the explicit text of the Qur'an and the hadith, as came in the hadith of the Night Journey, and as in His (ﷺ) saying to Sa'd: "You have judged by the judgment of the King from above seven heavens," and other texts of the Law.

The majority read ﴿mithlahunna﴾ (the like of them) in the accusative. Al-Mufaddal from 'Asim, and 'Isma from Abu Bakr, read ﴿mithluhunna﴾ in the nominative and then the accusative. Al-Zamakhshari said: "it is coordinated with ﴿seven heavens﴾." End of quotation. This involves separating the conjunction (the waw) from the conjoined term by a prepositional phrase, which is considered permissible only in poetic necessity according to Abu 'Ali al-Farisi. Some grammarians supposed a governing verb after the waw, indicated by what precedes it, meaning "and He created of the earth the like of them," so ﴿mithlahunna﴾ is the object of the omitted verb, not a coordinated term, and this becomes coordination of clauses. The nominative reading is on the basis of the inchoative, with ﴿min al-ardi﴾ (of the earth) as the predicate.

The sense of likeness can be true through sharing some attributes. The majority said that the likeness is in number, meaning that they are like them in being seven earths. In the hadith: "He will be hung with a collar from seven earths," and "Lord of the seven earths and what they carry." It was said: they are seven layers without gaps. It was said: there is a distance between each layer and the next. It was said: in them are inhabitants of God's creation. It was said: angels and jinn. On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, from the narration of al-Waqidi the liar, he said: "In every earth there is an Adam like Adam, a Noah like Noah, a prophet like your prophet, an Abraham like your Abraham, and a Jesus like Jesus." This is a narration with no doubt about its being fabricated. Abu Salih said: they are seven earths spread out, none above another, separated by seas, and the sky shades all of them.

﴿The command descends among them﴾: from the seven heavens to the seven earths. Muqatil and others said: the command here is revelation, so "among them" refers to the space between this earth, which is the nearest of them, and the seventh heaven. Most scholars said: the command is the decree, so "among them" refers to the space between the lowest earth, which is the farthest, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was also said: "the command descends among them" refers to life and death, wealth and poverty. It was also said: it is what is administered within them of wondrous governance.

The majority read ﴿yatanazzalu﴾ (descends), the present tense of tanazzala. 'Isa and Abu 'Amr, and in one narration, read ﴿yunazzilu﴾, the present tense of the doubled form nazzala, with ﴿al-amr﴾ (the command) in the accusative. The majority read ﴿li-ta'lamu﴾ (that you may know) with the second-person "ta." It is also read with the third-person "ya," and God knows best.
